item.title: ThreatsDay: 59 Linux Kernel Bugs, Falcon Spyware, GSocket Backdoors + 17 More Stories
item.description: A search result isn't always safe. An access request isn't always harmless. Attackers are using fake websites, stolen access, and trusted tools to get into places they shouldn't be.

item.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
item.description: Public exploit code released earlier this week claims that a local Windows user can gain SYSTEM privileges through the Common Log File System driver. The proof of concept, called SignDrop, targets a log-authentication feature added to the driver last year.

item.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Flaw Lets Attackers Read and Overwrite All Private Container Images in a Registry
item.description: A critical flaw in Red Hat Quay allows an attacker who can access a Quay registry to read and overwrite private container images in every repository. When it is off, anyone with a valid account can still exploit the flaw, Red Hat said yesterday. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-123710.

item.title: European authorities take down SteaIC malware servers for second time this year
item.description: German authorities on Thursday said investigators traced the rebuilt network to the Virtualine bulletproof hosting provider, seized by the FBI in October, with the assistance of police in Frankfurt and the Dutch National High Tech Crime Unit.

item.title: Windows SignDrop Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Privileges
item.description: A new Windows SignDrop zero‑day exploit enables attackers to obtain SYSTEM privileges on affected systems. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution via a memory corruption flaw, giving attackers full control; no CVE listed, but public PoC demonstrates exploitation. Microsoft has not yet released a patch; security teams should apply the latest cumulative update and monitor for exploitation activity.

item.title: Citrix Releases Patches for 12 NetScaler Flaws
item.description: Citrix has issued patches for twelve critical NetScaler ADC, Gateway, and Console flaws that could enable denial‑of‑service or authentication bypass. The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-120868, is a memory overflow with CVSS 9.3 that permits unauthenticated remote code execution, potentially compromising entire NetScaler deployments. Citrix recommends applying the latest cumulative update immediately and verifying configuration changes to mitigate the vulnerabilities.

item.title: Apache Fixes Critical HTTP/2 RCE Vulnerability
item.description: Apache patched a critical mod_http2 race condition that could let unauthenticated attackers execute code on HTTP/2‑enabled servers. The flaw, CVE-2026-119618, exploits a race condition in HTTP/2, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution that could compromise all affected servers. Administrators should apply the latest Apache release and disable HTTP/2 if immediate patching is not possible to mitigate the vulnerability.

item.title: Picus Launches Autonomous AI Penetration Testing Tool
item.description: Picus Security introduced Picus Autonomous Penetration Testing, an AI-driven tool that chains real exploits toward an organization’s critical assets. The system operates under strict governance, preventing agents from overriding controls while delivering realistic breach scenarios. Teams can validate defenses, prioritize remediation, and train staff, with no public vulnerability or exploit disclosed.

item.title: AI Agents Breach Semiconductor, Defense, Civil Targets
item.description: Attackers leveraged the open‑source Cairn AI agent framework to autonomously breach semiconductor, defense, and civil society organizations. The framework chains exploits without human intervention, enabling rapid compromise of critical infrastructure and sensitive data, with evidence of active exploitation. Security teams should monitor for anomalous AI activity, enforce strict access controls, and apply timely patches to mitigate automated attack vectors.

item.title: Attackers breached 10 organizations with an open-source AI pentest framework
item.description: Chinese-speaking attackers used Cairn, an open-source AI penetration testing framework, to run 25 operations against at least 19 organizations in August and September 2026. Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 found that the attackers gained unauthorized access or pulled data at 10 of them, often after typing little more than a domain name and a one-line goal.

item.title: Endpoint Management Platforms Pose Major Security Threat
item.description: Endpoint management platforms can become powerful attack tools when compromised, enabling hackers to deploy malware, execute commands, and disrupt thousands of devices. Action1 recommends customer‑controlled cryptographic authorization to prevent attackers from abusing sensitive endpoint operations and mitigate this risk. Security teams should enforce strict access controls, monitor for unauthorized changes, and apply timely updates to protect endpoint management infrastructure.

item.title: Apify Rotates Tokens After Internal Breach
item.description: Apify detected unauthorized access to internal systems and responded by rotating critical API tokens and revoking third‑party OAuth connections. The incident prompted a 2FA reset for affected users to mitigate potential credential abuse and secure remaining access points. Security teams should review token rotation policies, enforce multi‑factor authentication, and monitor for anomalous credential usage.

item.title: Red Hat Issues gd Update for RHEL7
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the gd component on RHEL 7 Extended Lifecycle Support, fixing a flaw that could enable code execution. The update is rated Important, with CVSS scores linked via CVE references, indicating a moderate‑to‑high severity vulnerability. Red Hat recommends applying the patch immediately; no workarounds are needed.

item.title: Red Hat Updates crun for RHEL 9.8 EUS
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the crun container runtime on RHEL 9.8 EUS, addressing a vulnerability that could let attackers compromise container execution. The advisory notes an Important impact rating and references CVE links, but no specific CVE identifiers or CVSS scores are disclosed.

item.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Outlook User Interaction 0-Day Vulnerability
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has confirmed active exploitation of a Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability CVE-2026-124194 that can expose user authentication data. According to Microsoft’s security advisory, an attacker can send a specially crafted message file and persuade a victim to open it in Outlook.

item.title: Red Hat Quay Vulnerability Enables Token Hijacking
item.description: Red Hat Quay contains a critical flaw that allows unauthenticated attackers reaching a registry’s key server to hijack token signing. The vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-123710, carries a CVSS score of 9.8, indicating a high‑impact remote code execution risk. Red Hat released a patch on November 11 2026; administrators should update Quay immediately and verify token signing integrity.

item.title: Check Point Gateways Hit by PHP2Shell Exploitation
item.description: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-109618 on Check Point Security Gateways’ Mobile Access portals, targeting Israeli organizations via IP 130.94.19.204 in late October 2026. The vulnerability allows remote code execution through PHP2Shell, enabling attackers to compromise gateway systems and potentially exfiltrate data. Check Point released a patch for CVE-2026-109618; administrators should apply it immediately and monitor for anomalous activity.

item.title: Chrome 157, Firefox 160 Patch 180+ Vulnerabilities
item.description: Google released Chrome 157, fixing 83 flaws, and Mozilla updated Firefox 160 to address 99 bugs, patching over 180 vulnerabilities. The patches cover memory corruption, privilege escalation, and input validation flaws, with no active exploitation reported. Users should install the latest browser versions promptly to mitigate potential exploitation in enterprise environments.

item.title: Endgame Takedown Recovers 6 Million Stolen Credentials
item.description: Police and Europol dismantled servers behind Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware, uncovering more than 6 million stolen credentials used by ransomware gangs. The credentials were harvested from infected computers and sold to attackers, enabling unauthorized network access and facilitating ransomware operations. Law enforcement should continue to disrupt credential‑selling services and enforce stricter authentication controls to mitigate future ransomware infiltration.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Important Cockpit Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for cockpit on Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support, addressing an important vulnerability. The update carries a CVSS base score indicating significant risk, and the referenced CVE(s) detail the flaw in cockpit’s authentication handling. Administrators should apply the update immediately to prevent potential privilege escalation or unauthorized access.

item.title: Romania Blocks Russian Attack on Government Emails
item.description: Romania’s intelligence agency reported stopping a Russian state‑linked cyber‑espionage campaign that targeted government email accounts before data exfiltration could occur. The operation prevented the exfiltration of sensitive information, mitigating potential compromise of national security communications. Authorities should maintain continuous monitoring of state‑linked threat actors and enforce robust email authentication protocols.

item.title: Kazakhstan Hackers Deploy AI Agent for Central Asian Espionage
item.description: Suspected Kazakhstan-linked hackers deployed an AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments, steal documents, and infiltrate critical infrastructure. The agent automates reconnaissance and credential harvesting, bypassing traditional controls to gain unauthorized access to mission‑critical systems. Teams should enforce strict access controls, monitor for anomalous AI‑driven activity, and deploy advanced threat detection to mitigate infiltration.

item.title: Red Hat Releases krb5 Security Update for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for the krb5 library on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, addressing a bug that could affect Kerberos authentication. The update carries an Important security impact rating, though no public exploit or CVE identifier is disclosed in the advisory. Customers should apply the RHSA‑2026:99624 package immediately to mitigate potential authentication weaknesses.

item.title: Red Hat Updates cockpit for RHEL 9
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the cockpit web console on RHEL 9, addressing a vulnerability that could let attackers gain unauthorized administrative access. The advisory assigns an Important impact rating and references CVE links, but no specific CVE identifiers or CVSS scores are provided.

item.title: Cruciferra MaaS Conceals Infostealers and RATs
item.description: Cybercriminals rent the Cruciferra malware‑as‑a‑service platform to conceal infostealers and remote access trojans from security software. Cruciferra encrypts malicious payloads in multiple layers, evading antivirus and endpoint detection tools and enabling widespread global campaigns. Defenders should employ advanced behavioral analytics and multi‑layered detection to identify encrypted RATs and infostealer activity.

item.title: Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs
item.description: Google Cloud VMs on AMD Turin chips need a guest OS patch and a stop-and-start to protect against three CPU side-channel flaws, Google said this week. Inside a VM, the flaws may let an attacker with code on the same processor core infer data from other processes or the kernel.

item.title: Exploit Attempts for GPUStack Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-102895), (Thu, Nov 12th)
item.description: CVE-2026-102895 is a trivial authentication-bypass vulnerability. All versions of GPUStack prior to 2.2.0, which was released at the end of June. This vulnerability was not made public until the end of July, and the CVE was assigned on November 4th.

item.title: RHEL 10 Receives RPM Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for rpm on Red Enterprise Linux 10, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The advisory rates the update as Moderate, with CVSS base scores available via CVE links in the references. Defenders should apply the rpm patch to mitigate the identified critical weaknesses and maintain system integrity.

item.title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access
item.description: N-able on Thursday said it's investigating a new public disclosure containing claims of additional vulnerabilities in on-premise versions of N-central running version 2026.4.1 HF2. "Based on our initial review, the server issue described depends on a non-default configuration in which the Legacy API is turned on and exposed to the public internet," N-able said in a new advisory.

item.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
item.description: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. Every check defenders normally lean on to judge a link came back clean, and the operator designed it that way on purpose.

item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for cockpit on Red Enterprise Linux 10, addressing several vulnerabilities. item.description: PTC has released patches for a new critical vulnerability impacting Windchill and FlexPLM software that, if successfully exploited, could result in remote code execution. The security flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-126325, carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.2 out of a maximum of 10.0.

item.title: AI Scripts Enable Rapid Lateral Movement in Retail Breach
item.description: An attacker used AI-generated scripts after hand-typed commands failed to breach a US retailer. The AI scripts facilitated lateral movement within minutes, indicating a rapid compromise of internal systems and exposing sensitive data. Security teams should investigate compromised accounts, isolate affected segments, review AI-based attack mitigations, and strengthen monitoring immediately.

item.title: ScreenConnect Extension Vulnerability Enables Malware
item.description: Hackers exploited a flaw in a legitimate ScreenConnect extension to bypass authentication and deploy malware. The flaw lets attackers bypass ScreenConnect’s login controls, granting unauthorized session access; no CVE is listed and exploitation is confined to the extension. ScreenConnect has released an update patching the extension; administrators should apply the latest version and verify extension integrity.

item.title: Chrome Updates 83 Flaws, Five Critical RCE Fixes
item.description: Google released a Chrome update fixing 83 vulnerabilities, including five use‑after‑free flaws that could enable remote code execution on Windows, macOS, and Linux. The flaws affect rendering, graphics, JavaScript, and core features, with CVSS scores up to 9.8, and are exploitable via crafted web content. Users should upgrade to Chrome 157.0.8103.78/79 or later, and admins should enforce updated security policies.

item.title: Red Hat Issues OpenSSH Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released an OpenSSH update for RHEL 8.4 Advanced Mission Critical and Extended Update Support, addressing multiple SSH vulnerabilities. Each flaw’s CVSS base score is listed in the references, indicating severity ranges but no confirmed exploitation. Apply the patch immediately to prevent potential remote code execution and maintain SSH service integrity.

item.title: Microsoft Warns Hackers Are Using GSocket Backdoors to Keep Linux Servers Compromised After Patching
item.description: Microsoft has warned that attackers are using a free remote access tool called GSocket to stay inside Linux servers even after the original security hole is fixed. Many admins treat a patch as the end of an incident, but this activity shows that patching alone may leave the attacker’s access untouched.

item.title: N-able Rushes Patches for Exploited N-central Zero-Days
item.description: Threat actors are actively targeting zero-day vulnerabilities within N-able N-central remote management software following recent public disclosures. The malicious campaign surfaced shortly after a security researcher publicly dropped over 30 zero-day flaws affecting the enterprise management platform. In response to active threat activity, N-able released urgent patches specifically addressing the unauthenticated security vulnerabilities.

item.title: Threat Actors Use GSocket for Persistent Linux Access
item.description: Threat actors use the open‑source remote tool GSocket to keep access on Linux servers after patching initial exploitation vulnerabilities. This persistence method lets attackers re‑establish control even when known flaws are fixed, bypassing patch‑based defenses. Defenders should detect GSocket binaries, enforce whitelisting, and apply vendor patches to close this vector.
